title: Architecture Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance, and ADRs
author: Priya Shah
body:
Purpose

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's canonical architecture and engineering standards across API design, coding, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, and performance. It also summarizes related decision records (ADRs) and provides actionable checklists for design reviews and production rollouts. The goal is to reduce design drift, improve interoperability across teams, and ensure predictable SLO compliance for production inference services.

Scope

Applies to: Redwood-hosted services, Dedicated control plane, and Private deployment reference architecture. Excludes: experimental research prototypes (placed in applied-ml-and-evals) and marketing artifacts.

Owners and contacts

- Standards steward: Priya Shah (architecture-and-standards)
- API standards owner: Evan Martinez (eng-developer-experience)
- Model-serving standards owner: Sara Liu (eng-serving-runtime)
- Observability and SRE liaison: Diego Fernández (eng-sre)
- Questions/PRs: open an RFC in the architecture Slack channel and link to a GH PR against infra/coding-standards repo.

High-level principles

1) Developer ergonomics: APIs must be predictable, discoverable, and have clear error semantics.
2) Production-first: every design must include SLOs, rollback plans, and a monitoring + alerting checklist.
3) Composability: services should expose small, versioned contracts; prefer HTTP+JSON/Protobuf for inter-service comms.
4) Cost-awareness: design decisions should include expected cost impact and quantifiable metrics (tokens/sec, GPU-hours, egress).

API standards (REST and gRPC)

- Surface: All public-facing endpoints must have OpenAPI (v3) or proto definitions stored in the api-definitions repo.
- Versioning: Use path versioning (/v1/..., /v2/...) for semantic breaking changes. Minor behavior changes must be behind feature flags.
- Authentication: Bearer token via Authorization header; service-to-service uses mTLS and JWTs issued by our internal auth service.
- Error model: Follow problem+json spec with fields {type, title, status, detail, instance, retryAfter?}. Retryable errors must set Retry-After.
- Pagination: cursor-based (next_cursor) for large lists. Avoid offset for large-scale datasets.
- Rate limits: documented per-route, implement quota-aware headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset.

Example OpenAPI snippet (simplified):

POST /v1/generate
Request: {
  "model": "redwood-7b-v2",
  "prompt": "<string>",
  "max_tokens": 256
}
Response 200: {"request_id":"<uuid>", "tokens": [ ... ] }

Coding standards and repository hygiene

- Languages: Primary backend languages = Go (core runtime, control plane), Python (SDKs, experiments), TypeScript (console/frontend).
- Formatting/linters: Enforce gofmt/goimports, golangci-lint; Black + ruff for Python; eslint + prettier for TypeScript.
- Testing: Unit tests target >80% coverage for critical path modules (scheduling, KV cache, auth). Integration tests required for model-serving interfaces and end-to-end request flows.
- PR requirements: descriptive title, linked issue or RFC, tests, changelog entry (if public API), and at least one reviewer from owner_team. CI must pass with no flaky tests.
- Dependency policy: Dependabot alerts enabled; major upgrades require an ADR if they change runtime semantics.

Infrastructure standards

- IaC: Terraform is the canonical source for cloud infra; modules must live in terraform-modules repo. Use remote state and enforce locking.
- Network: Zero-trust principles; all traffic between services in cloud uses VPC peering plus service-level mTLS. Cloud subnets: control-plane (private), serving-plane (GPU subnets), logging/metrics (restricted).
- Secrets: KMS-backed secrets. For Private deployments, recommend HSM integration; never store plaintext secrets in state or logs.
- Capacity and autoscaling: Define target utilization per pool (e.g., GPU utilization target 60-70%); autoscale rules must include cooldowns and max/min capacity.

Model-serving standards

- Model packaging: canonical model manifest = model.yaml with fields: name, version, dtype, quantization_profile, required_kv_cache, max_context. Manifests declared in model-catalog repo.
- Serving contract: All serving instances must implement a stable gRPC contract for inference that includes streaming, abort semantics, and per-request metadata (request_id, principal, trace_id).
- Fallbacks: For transient capacity issues, route to fallback model variants (smaller/quantized) with documented quality degradation bounds.
- Warmup & KV cache: Warmup sequence must be defined for models that use large KV caches. Default warmup policy: preload last N popular prefixes for 10 minutes after scale-up.

Observability standards

- Tracing: Use W3C Trace Context across services. Span conventions: service.name, endpoint, model.name, model.version, batch.size, tokens.generated.
- Metrics: Prometheus with standard labels (service, route, model, region, shard). Key metrics: request_latency_ms_p50/p95/p99, tokens_per_second, batch_size_histogram, model_cache_hit_rate, gpu_utilization.
- Dashboards and alerts: Per-route latency (p99 > 300ms) -> page oncall. Error rate > 0.5% for 5m -> alert. Model regression alerting hooks wired to Redwood Optimize evals.
- Logs: Structured JSON logs with level, timestamp, request_id, trace_id, route, model, error_code. Retention: 90 days for standard, configurable for enterprise customers.

Performance and SLOs

- Standard SLOs (default for hosted routes unless overridden by contract):
  - Availability: 99.95% monthly
  - P95 latency: <= 200ms for small prompt (<=128 tokens)
  - P99 latency: <= 500ms for small prompt
  - Token throughput per GPU: documented in model catalog per model/quantization profile
- Error budget: calculated at service level; require postmortem after consuming >25% of monthly error budget.
- Load testing: New model/version requires perf validation with 95th and 99th percentile measurements across target regions and expected prompt distributions.

Decision records (ADRs) summary

- ADR-2025-04: Standardize on path versioning for public APIs (adopted).
- ADR-2025-09: Use gRPC for intra-service model streaming (adopted).
- ADR-2026-01: Default quantization profiles and storage formats (rejected: deferred to model-catalog per-model).
- ADR-2026-07: Observability schema (adopted): adopt W3C trace context and canonical metric names.

Checklist for design review and production rollout

1) Architecture review: include owners for API, infra, serving, SRE, security. 2) SLOs defined and measurable. 3) OpenAPI/proto and SDK compatibility verified. 4) IaC changes reviewed, remote state plan provided. 5) Chaos and failure-mode testing plan documented. 6) Rollback strategy and canary configuration defined. 7) Observability: dashboards, alerts, log parsing ready. 8) Security review: threat model, auth, secrets handling.

Example canary rollout steps (recommended)

1) Deploy new model/service to a staging cluster with identical metrics pipeline. 2) Run synthetic traffic for 1 hour to validate latency and correctness. 3) Canary: route 1% production traffic for 30 minutes, monitor errors and p99 latency. 4) If no regressions, ramp to 10% for 1 hour, then 50% for 2 hours. 5) Verify SLOs and user-facing metrics; promote to 100% or rollback.

Related artifacts and repositories

- api-definitions (OpenAPI/protos)
- terraform-modules
- model-catalog (manifests and quantization-profiles)
- infra-monitoring (dashboards/alerts)
- ci-templates (PR checklists, linting pipelines)

Appendix: Example model.yaml manifest

name: redwood-7b-v2
version: 2026-03-01
dtype: float16
quantization_profile: q4_0
max_context: 8192
required_kv_cache: true
owned_by: eng-serving-runtime

Notes and future work

- We will publish a machine-readable schema (JSON Schema) for model manifests in Q1 2027.
- Continue standardizing SDK error types to make client retries deterministic.
- Investigate standardized cost-metering headers for model billing visibility.
